accepted.question_text: For a given Grothendieck topos, consider the connected surjective geometric morphisms with that topos as domain, where these actual quotients are determined by left exact comonads that are idempotent. Does there exist a Grothendieck topos for which the collection of such quotients is not small?

evidence.quote: But how many are those morphisms that, by analogy with the topological special case, are called "connected surjective"? These actual quotients are determined by left exact comonads that are moreover idempotent. Is there a Grothendieck topos for which the number of these quotients is not small?

accepted.question_text: For the connected surjective geometric morphisms that serve as actual quotients of a Grothendieck topos, can those quotients be parameterized internally in a way analogous to the internal parameterization of subtoposes?

evidence.quote: At the other extreme, could they be parameterized internally, as subtoposes are?

accepted.question_text: Let the coherently idempotent left exact endofunctors on a given topos be viewed as parameterizing its subquotients, with a lattice structure and two closure operators: one sending a subquotient to the smallest subtopos containing its inverse image, and the other sending a subtopos to the smallest quotient for which the composite is an inclusion. What algebraic properties does this lattice have when equipped with those two closure operators, which retract onto the quotient-type and inclusion-type special subquotients respectively?

evidence.quote: What are the algebraic properties of this lattice equipped with two closure operators, retracting respectively onto the two kinds of special subquotients?

accepted.question_text: Subtoposes of any topos form a co-Heyting algebra with a boundary operator defined by contradiction and also a double-negation core operator. Since subtoposes represent classes of models of positive extensions of a given theory, determine both semantically and syntactically how the boundary operator and the double-negation core operator act on such classes of models.
accepted.context_brief: Boundary and double-negation on model classes

evidence.quote: Because subtoposes represent classes of models of positive extensions of a given theory, the effect of the boundary operator (and of the double negation core operator) on classes of models needs to be determined both semantically and syntically.

accepted.question_text: In the Boolean algebra classifier, described here as the topos of presheaves on the category of finite non-empty sets, the essential subtoposes or levels correspond to natural numbers together with minus infinity, and the resulting chain conditions ensure that a jump operator exists. What is the way-below relation between levels in this basic topos, expressed in combinatorial or number-theoretic terms?

evidence.quote: There is another fundamental topos related to classical constructions and combinatorial topology, namely the Boolean algebra classifier that consists of presheaves on the category of finite non-empty sets. Here again, the levels correspond to natural numbers (together with minus infinity), so that there are sufficient chain conditions to ensure that the jump operator exists. What is, in combinatorial or number theoretic terms, the way below relation for this basic topos?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a covering A → B in the category of finitely presented K-rigs is defined by the existence of an averaging process from B onto A, meaning a retraction in the category of A-modules. The resulting sheaf topos has some of the good properties of micro-linear objects while remaining a topos. In general, what is the relation between micro-linearity and coverings of this averaging type?

evidence.quote: In general, what is the relation between micro-linearity and these coverings?

accepted.question_text: When a Grothendieck topology is defined using coverings A → B that admit averaging with respect to a weaker structure than the one classified by the site, are there examples beyond the finitely presented K-rig setting where this method still produces a meaningful Grothendieck topology?

evidence.quote: Are there other examples where a Grothendieck topology can be defined in this way by averaging with respect to structure that is weaker than that classified by the site?

accepted.question_text: Can an analogue of the averaging-based covering construction be developed for C-infinity functions together with distributions of compact support?
accepted.context_brief: Averaging with smooth functions and distributions

evidence.quote: Can something similar be done with C-infinity functions and distributions of compact support?

accepted.question_text: How does the particular example of a Grothendieck topology generated by coverings that admit averaging fit within the broader family of Grothendieck topologies that have traditionally been useful in algebraic geometry?

evidence.quote: How does the above particular example fit into the family of Grothendieck topologies traditionally useful in algebraic geometry?

accepted.question_text: Let an ATOM in a topos mean an object D such that exponentiation by D, written ( )^D, has a right adjoint ( )^(1/D). For any finite set of ATOMs there is a lower topos of relatively discrete objects over which those defining adjunctions and their corresponding fractional exponents are enriched. Can the entire class of all ATOMs be parameterized in a suitable way, and can one define a lower topos over which all of these adjunctions are simultaneously enriched?

evidence.quote: Can the class of all ATOMs be suitably parameterized and can we define a lower topos over which all these adjunctions are enriched? (Recall that ATOMs are objects D for which ( )ˆD has a right adjoint ( )ˆ1/D; the term (distinct from Barr’s above Boolean notion) was used in Bunge’s thesis to help characterize presheaf categories, but such objects occur in more general contexts where they sometimes play the role of Amazingly Tiny Objectified Motion, the fractional exponent being a special case of the additional functor, characteristic of a local geometric morphism, that Grothendieck denoted with a superscript exclamation point.)

accepted.question_text: Let D → A be a map in a topos where D is an ATOM. Writing F(U) for the left-adjoint construction that parameterizes solutions of the corresponding prolongation equations over a time interval U as motions, can the Algebra of Time F(U) be computed explicitly in familiar terms?
accepted.context_brief: Explicit form of the Algebra of Time

evidence.quote: Can the Algebra of Time F(U) be calculated in familiar terms ?
